analysis:
All units in this batch are documentation only; no Swift implementation was supplied.

model-autopilot.md (head 5-10, 37-255) changes the documented consent contract. With saved consent, the Autopilot set is no longer only the explicit selection. It also includes every verified catalog build in the cache, plus builds the coordinator downloads on the operator's behalf. Downloads are on by default (head 86-100): no storage or model cap by default, and a 50 GiB free-disk reserve. Adoption (head 151) admits models to serving without a lease or an ordinary selection.

Without a catalog, verification falls back to the owner-only autopilot-downloads.json ledger hash (head 63, 136-138). That file is writable by the operator, who is adversarial (ADV-001, TB-003). Weight integrity is unchanged in kind, because A-004, T-012 and T-027 already treat local weights as operator-controlled. Still, integration should confirm that the coordinator never treats the provider-reported ledger hash as stronger evidence than the catalog weight_hash.

Coordinator-initiated downloads are new provider disk and network surface. They are only partly covered by T-016, and they compete with the SSD prefix cache's available/2 budget and 20 GiB reserve (T-041). The documented 50 GiB reserve and 'unknown free space refuses' rule (head 126) limit exhaustion, but code was not seen. The coordinator is trusted, so download triggering by it is not an adversarial boundary. Consumers have no documented path to trigger downloads.

The new telemetry fields (telemetry.md head 34-44) are typed, closed-vocabulary busy/stall fields that carry no prompt data, so no A-001 exposure. The cli-reference changes document `downloads enable/disable`, which do not change the consent revision or lease.

Integration must check against the implementation:
- The 256-ID set bound.
- Refusal of prefetch without consent or with downloads off.
- That adoption ends on revocation or a failed self-test.
- Download path and ID validation (1-256 bytes of visible ASCII).
- That downloads never touch native admission or App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052).

The threat model has no Autopilot entry. Maintainers may want to add the download, ledger and adoption surface. No concrete regression is provable from docs alone.
